# Josie Pye

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. ## Appearance

Josie Pye is known for her stylish wardrobe, particularly during the autumn season. She wears dresses that feature flounces on every garment.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)_

## Personality

Josie Pye is known for her disagreeable nature and sharp tongue, though she lacks imagination. Highly skilled at walking board fences and talented in making knitted lace, she plans to attend college purely for the sake of education since she does not need to earn a living.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. ## History

Josie Pye attended the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school as the last member of her family to go there. Possessing a natural gift for walking board fences, she used her skill to challenge [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) during a game of dares at Diana's party, daring [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof. Josie was also known for her needlework talents, having won first prize for knitted lace at an exhibition. Later in her schooling, she traveled to town alongside her [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) classmates to take the [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examinations for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy). After passing, she attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy) in town along with her peers. During her time there, Josie visited [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) alongside [Jane](../character/jane.md) and Ruby to share news of the Avery scholarship.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "Queen’s is to get one of the Avery scholarships after all. The word came today. Frank Stockley told me—his uncle is one of the board of governors, you know. It will be announced in the Academy tomorrow."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl P24](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0024)

> "If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next. My father can afford to send me. Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P14](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0014)

> "I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)

> "I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. You couldn’t, anyhow."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)

> "Are you going to be back next year, Miss Stacy?"
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P30](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0030)
